page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-24 belongs to the network-optimized C4N instance family, designed to support processing pipelines with substantial data transfer needs. The virtual machine runs on the x86_64 architecture and supplies 24 dedicated vCPUs backed by 90 GB of total memory. This configuration establishes a balanced ratio of 3.75 GB of memory per core, ensuring consistent computational execution across parallel processing tasks.

In terms of storage and hardware acceleration, the instance does not bundle local storage disks or discrete GPUs. All persistent file systems and disk operations must be handled using external block storage options. The configuration also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard virtual private cloud routing configurations or external IP assignments for public connectivity.

From an architectural perspective, the provision of dedicated vCPUs guarantees uninterrupted compute resources without the throttling risks associated with burstable systems. Forgoing integrated local disks offers cost efficiency for applications that prioritize centralized or network-attached persistent storage. The configuration fits workloads such as network proxy servers, container orchestration nodes, backend web applications, and distributed middleware.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-24 is a network-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 processor architecture. It is equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs and 90 GB of system memory, establishing a memory density of 3.75 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage disks, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data, and operates without discrete GPU accelerators. It also provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Engineered for predictable performance, the instance avoids shared-resource contention through dedicated compute allocation. Resource spending is focused strictly on CPU and system memory rather than bundled disk hardware, providing architectural efficiency for storage-independent or remote-storage deployments. The c4n-standard-24 is suited for network-intensive application gateways, distributed middleware, web serving clusters, ETL microservices, and general-purpose enterprise application backends requiring consistent multi-core capacity.
